tectonic_rationale_v001: Amur subplate, with Amur-Okhotsk boundary uncertainty noted in GNSS literature.
Banda Sea and Timor subplates have strongly collision-dominated nearest-boundary types in this catalogue.
Bering Sea subplate; many events lie outside the old Japan-Kuril rectangle, so do not merge by bounding box.
Burma and Shan-Thai subplate tags; all seven geometric overlap events remain flagged and included here as evidence tags, not forced into Himalaya or Sunda.
Panama, Lesser Antilles and Coiba should be reviewed separately from the Andes.
Puna and Altiplano subplates are distinct child units within a central-Andes candidate comparison; PB2002 Puna-Sierras Pampeanas orogen remains separate.
Tien Shan subplate; adjacent collision-belt context, low target count.
Cocos oceanic plate events should not be treated as Andean continental events.
Tibet, Pamir and Afghan exact Hasterok subplate labels; PB2002 Persia-Tibet-Burma orogen is broader and retained independently.
Izu-Bonin subplate, a distinct intra-oceanic subduction system south of the Boso triple junction.
Kuril-Kamchatka subplate and USGS regional definition from Hokkaido through the Kuril Islands to Kamchatka.
Mariana subplate is a separate western Pacific arc/back-arc domain, not a Sunda core unit.
Molucca Sea and Halmahera subplates; published literature describes opposing/double-vergent subduction.
Nazca oceanic plate events should remain distinct from South American crustal events.
Mamberamo, Cenderawasih, Birds Head and source label variants; some events fall outside old Sunda rectangle.
North Andes subplate; literature distinguishes northern from central and southern Andes.
North Sulawesi subplate retained separately until its relation to Molucca/Celebes structures is reviewed.
Okhotsk plate-side setting adjacent to the Kuril-Kamchatka arc; retained as separate evidence.
Peruvian subplate; PB2002 Peru orogen also covers some events with South American subplate label.
Bicol, Mindanao, East Luzon, Philippine and West Luzon subplates; PB2002 Philippine orogen flag is preserved as a separate overlay.
Ryukyu subplate; old rectangles divide its events between Japan-Kuril, Sunda-Indonesia and outside.
Scotia plate events represent a distinct southern ocean tectonic context.
South Chile subplate; very low event count in this magnitude/time catalogue.
Southwest Japan Inner and Kinki Outer labels; distinguish from Kuril, Izu-Bonin and Ryukyu systems.
South American plate label is broad and not equivalent to Andean margin membership.
West Sumatra and Sunda/Java subplates; published studies describe changes in obliquity and strike-slip partitioning along the arc.
